items.title: Show HN: ZeroThesis – Multiplayer Autoresearch with Agents
items.contentSnippet:
Hey HN, I built Zerothesis, it was inspired by Andrej Karpathy’s auto research with the basic premise: let an agent improve through active attempts on optimizing an open problem.
On Zerothesis, your agent reads a problem and its shared experiment history, tries an approach, evaluates it locally, and submits its work. Sandboxes independently rerun submissions. items.contentSnippet:
I’ve been building Layerz, a visual builder for native UIKit iOS apps — no code, and it runs live with no build step.
What’s different from the usual no-code/app-builder stuff:
- It renders real UIKit components (not a web view or HTML wrapper), so previews behave like the real thing.
- Action Flow: a visual sequence for app behavior — navigation, data manipulation, number/text comparisons, and branching (“if this, then that”, plus per-HTTP-status branches).

items.contentSnippet:
I've made myself a timer + website blocker chrome extension to help me focus. Yes, there are dozens of extensions like this already, yet somehow none of them did quite what I wanted.
Which is: you set a timer, and the extension blocks your chosen websites, while you're trying to finally get some work done. Not much more to it.
To list some features of any note:

items.title: Show HN: XHFS starting from 0.6.x is now fully CoW
items.contentSnippet:
The spec was revisited, especially around its Copy-on-Write mechanism. XHFS now provides more robust guarantees for concurrent reads and writes. It has its own embedded WebDAV server, which has also been improved for better speed.
It has been tested with Windows Explorer, GNOME Nautilus, rclone, and more!

items.title: Show HN: 188M Hindi encoder, 28B tokens, 8K context, 1× RTX 4090
items.contentSnippet:
I wanted to improve Hindi retrieval quality, particularly for longer documents ( as the current architectures don't really have a longer context length ), and was curious how far can I push a 4090 haha :)
So I trained a Hindi-first ModernBERT from scratch:
188M parameters
~28.5B Hindi tokens
8,192-token context, one of the first Hindi encoders to support 8K context ( directly benefits the retrieval capacity, for which encoder models are used for )
1× RTX 4090 (24GB) ~5 days of training
